digest.component_or_area: Gerrit Verify gate, corpus and external integration
propositions: Gerrit Verify performs complete live-Pandoc corpus replay on every change, contributing a measured 184.32-second macOS lower bound; the implementation must reduce per-change subprocess work while retaining all behavioral assertions and full replay capability elsewhere.

The implementation extends the corpus generator to produce deterministic committed artifacts covering all Pandoc-bound inputs through all settling passes, split by stratum and kept below file-size limits, preserving the Pandoc 3.6.1 contract and binary SHA-256 values for Linux x86_64 and Darwin arm64.

Gerrit Verify must drive the production renderer through a test-only static converter backed by committed artifacts for broad corpus assertions, while retaining one deterministic live product-path body from each code_arrow, table, and prose stratum plus compact version/platform/argv/stdin/timeout probes.

A dedicated external pandoc-corpus-replay job must execute every corpus unit and settling pass through real Pandoc on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest on a weekly schedule and workflow_dispatch, validating all 178 bodies, 1,383 conversions, and committed bytes deterministically.

The implementation achieved a 90.8% wall-time reduction in focused paired A/B testing (42s to 4s) while replacing per-change live replay with static assertions, proven by independent full external replay validation on real Pandoc 3.6.1.
